title: The Adventure Begins
premise: Keen sets out alone on his first sea voyage with his late father's vacant wristbands on his wrists; a storm strips away his map and his plan, and when Squeaky is dragged under by a drift net he dives anyway — and is carried back to a cove where a whole family is already lighting a beacon for him.
dramaticQuestion: Can Keen stop performing bravery long enough to actually be brave — and will he find out he was never out there on his own?
theme: Courage is not the absence of the gulp; it is the gulp swallowed and the step taken anyway — and it is never done alone. Bravado (Fuzzby's 'Nailed it.', Keen's 'Still got it!') is the same joke shape twice, and the real thing looks nothing like it.
externalJourney: Meadow pollen-round → Aida's vision at the cove → the pier goodbye and the wristband handoff → open water, map lost, lost at sea → the bees spot the boat → the bears' combined beacon → the underwater rescue of Squeaky → the ride in on the crest → the welcome on the sand → the Aquamarine awarded and set into the vacant bands → the honey-friendship walk home.
internalJourney: Keen begins over-checking straps because checking is what he does instead of admitting his paws are unsteady. Every prop that props him up is taken away — the map, the boat, the plan — until the only thing left is the vacant gold on his wrists and someone smaller than him who needs pulling free. He stops trying to look ready and simply pulls, and the bands answer from inside. By the end he is not braver-looking; he is held.
relationshipChanges: Mum's hands open — she goes from closing her paws around his to lifting one in a wave as he shrinks away. Squeaky moves from playmate to rescued to rescuer, carrying him in. Fuzzby's panic converts into worship of somebody else, which is new for him; Zenny pulls him back by the leg twice and it reads as care both times. Aida, who saw Keen in a bubble before she ever met him, ends the episode putting a crystal on him and calling it family.
emotionalCurve: Play (meadow silliness) → a hush of foreknowledge (Aida's vision) → warm ache (the pier, the empty gold) → bright then thinning confidence (open water) → fear with the horizon gone → alarm and mobilisation on land → the nadir, held and wordless underwater as his strength runs out and the bands answer → release, whoop, laughter → warmth of welcome → settled belonging with the trace of the morning still in it.
comedyCurve: Fuzzby's three-beat overcommitment opens the show and calibrates the joke shape; Zenny's 'Officially nuts!' is the first laugh. Keen inherits the shape at the dock ('Still got it!') and again with the upside-down map. Fuzzby's beach crash-landing ('I meant to do that.') re-fires it under real stakes. After the rescue the comedy converts from cover-up to pure delight — the early clap, the honey list — so the funny at the end is honest rather than defensive.
setupPayoffMap: Vacant wristbands pressed into his paws (S3) → faint self-glow underwater (S7) → Aquamarine gems settle into the same bezels (S9). 'Wherever you go… You'll never be alone.' from Mum (S3) → repeated by Aida to a whole circle (S9). Fuzzby's 'Nailed it.' (S1) → Keen's 'Still got it!' (S3) → Fuzzby's 'I meant to do that.' (S6). Distant thunder Zenny names (S1) → the storm that takes the map (S4). Squeaky named on the water (S4) → Squeaky carrying him home (S7). Aida's vision of the pier (S2) → Aida sending a message to Mum via Squeaky (S8), closing the loop the audience opened.
visualMotifs: Empty gold bezels and paws closing over them; straps checked one more time than necessary; the map turned upside down then gone; a small boat between two grey waves; light as beacon versus light as glow-from-within; a circle of bodies around one bear (the bear hug echoing the beacon huddle); Mum small on the dock and, later, Keen small under a wave.
sonicMotifs: Fuzzby's BUZZZZZZ-CRASH and Zenny's Ommmmm… ping open the world. Keen's note B sits alone and unresolved from the pier through the storm, thins to almost nothing underwater, and resolves to true pitch as the bands glow; Aida's G under the vision and the beacon; the seven notes stack into one chord on the combined Crystal Call; the singing bowl's rim-tone at the start rhymes with the crystal hum when the gems split. Rain, rope-creak and hull-knock replace all music at the nadir.
climax: Underwater, out of strength, with a wave massing above him: Keen sees the faint glow start inside his father's vacant bands, braces on a rock and tears the net — 'COME ON!' — and the sea explodes over them.
resolution: Aida awards the Aquamarine; it splits and settles into the two vacant bezels, Keen speaks his Crystal Call, and the group swamps him in a hug. Then the beach walk, Fuzzby's honey campaign, and everyone laughing as they go.
intendedFinalFeeling: Warm and belonged, with the morning's goodbye still faintly in the chest — a child grinning at the honey list while an adult remembers whose hands opened at the pier to make this possible.
